hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated sulfuric acid can do besides acting as an acid, it is also a strong oxidising agent.
Recall that reducing power increases down Group 17, so iodide is the strongest reductant and chloride is the weakest.
Think about which hydrogen halides are strong enough reductants to reduce sulfur from +6 to +4 or lower while being oxidised to X2 themselves.
walkthrough:
**Start with the acid-base reaction for all three**

All three potassium halides first react as acids and bases to make the hydrogen halide.

$$\text{KX(s) + H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(l) } \rightarrow \text{ KHSO}_4\text{(s) + HX(g)}$$

**Ask if the HX can be oxidised further**

Hot, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ can oxidise $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{HI}$ to $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$, but it cannot oxidise $\text{HCl}$.

This is because reducing power is $\text{I}^- > \text{Br}^- > \text{Cl}^-$.

**Write the oxidation products**

For bromide, orange-brown bromine vapour is seen with sulfur dioxide:
$$\text{2HBr + H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Br}_2 + \text{SO}_2 + \text{2H}_2\text{O}$$

For iodide, purple-black iodine vapour is seen with a mixture of sulfur products ($\text{SO}_2$, S, $\text{H}_2\text{S}$):
$$\text{8HI + H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{4I}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{4H}_2\text{O}$$

For chloride, the reaction stops at steamy white fumes of $\text{HCl}$, no $\text{Cl}_2$ forms.

**Conclude which statements are correct**

Statements 1 and 2 produce $\text{X}_2$, statement 3 does not. That combination is 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three. Potassium chloride gives only $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{KHSO}_4$. Chloride ion is too weak a reductant to reduce concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, so no $\text{Cl}_2$ is formed.
options.B: Correct because 1 and 2 only are true. Both $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ are strong enough reductants to be oxidised to $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$ while reducing $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to $\text{SO}_2$ and, for iodide, to S and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ as well.
options.C: Incorrect because it pairs 2 and 3. While 2 is correct ($\text{Br}_2$ is formed), 3 is wrong as $\text{KCl}$ does not give $\text{Cl}_2$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes 1 only. Potassium iodide does give $\text{I}_2$, but potassium bromide also gives $\text{Br}_2$, so choosing 1 alone misses a valid halide.
